paper_title: Quantum PCPs: on Adaptivity, Multiple Provers and Reductions to Local Hamiltonians
authors: Harry Buhrman; Jonas Helsen; Jordi Weggemans
statement: For soundness, let ρ be the p2 (n)t-qubit proof that Merlin provides instead of ξ ⊗t . From the soundness property of the verifier, we know that E[X1 ] ≤ s. Now consider the expectation of X2 , which depends on the outcome of X1 . However, the soundness condition ensures that E[X2 | X1 = j] ≤ s for all possible outcomes j ∈ {0, 1}. By repeating this argument, we see that for any i, E[Xi | X1 , . . . , Xi−1 ] ≤ s. Since this holds for any i, we can upper bound the acceptance probability by polynomially many independent Bernoulli trials with mean µ = s, again with bias (c−s)/2. Applying a Chernoff bound for dependent variables (with bounded conditional expectations), we find that the acceptance probability is at most 2−t . Finally, the total number of queries to the proof is qR = O(qt). We leave open the question of weak error reduction for the multiple-prover case, but we expect that it can be done using the ideas in [26]. When we have near-perfect completeness, strong error reduction is also possible for non-adaptive quantum PCPs. Claim 1 (Strong error reduction for non-adaptive QPCPs with near-perfect completeness). For l ∈ O(1) it holds that QPCPNA [1, q, c, s] = QPCPNA [1, lq, c′ , s′ ] with c = 1 − 2−Ω(n) , s = 1/2 and c′ = 1 − 2−Ω(n) , s′ = 2−O(l) . The proof can be found in Appendix A.

The proof can be found in Appendix A. 4 Local Hamiltonians from quantum PCPs The core of this section is Theorem 1, which argues that we can, from a QPCP verification circuit (as in Definition 4) efficiently produce a local Hamiltonian, such that the expectation value of a proof state is given by its acceptance probability by the verifier. Our construction broadly follows the ideas in [21], but also includes the more general adaptive verifier case.
